subject: Islamic Studies
board: TGA Islamic Studies scheme (aqeedah, fiqh, seerah, hadith, akhlaq)
source: Adapted from TGA Drive RE/Islamic Studies folder (Al-Baseerah Salah quizzes EYFS-KS1/KS2: blessings, gratitude, amanah, best act after the shahadah, praying on time); National Curriculum RE (KS1) | Spring 1 2027 (lessons 7 and 8 upgraded, 13 new): TGA Year 1 Curriculum Pack (Islamic Studies Spring 1 weeks 1, 3, 5); hadith of the five pillars (Bukhari 8, Muslim 16); school-approved children's Islamic Studies texts TO CONFIRM

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Allah, the One and Only
lessons.title: Allah is One (Tawheed)
objectives: Explain that Allah is One and has no partner
Say the first two ayat of Surah al-Ikhlas
Say what 'Allah made everything' means

keywords.def: Lord: the One who made, owns and looks after us
someone who shares in what belongs to Allah

starter: Bismillah! Who made the sun, the moon and you?
What do we say when we see something amazing?
What do we say to thank Allah?

teach.heading: Allah is our Lord
teach.note: Begin with Bismillah. Ask: who made the world? Children say Allah. Explain that 'Rabb' means the Lord who makes, owns and cares. Allah says in the Qur'an that to Him belongs whatever is in the heavens and the earth (2:284).

teach.heading: Allah is One
bullets: Allah has no wife or children
teach.note: Say: Allah is One, nobody is like Him. Use one raised finger. Misconception: asking what Allah looks like. We never imagine or draw Allah. Say: nothing is like Allah (42:11).

teach.heading: Surah al-Ikhlas
bullets: Say: He is Allah, the One
Allah is the One everyone needs
teach.note: Recite the first two ayat slowly, children echo. 'As-Samad' means the One everyone needs, but He needs no one. Give the English for each ayah. Say that this surah is all about Allah being One.

teach.heading: Only Allah is worshipped
teach.note: Link to salah. Ask: who do we say thank you to for food? Accept Allah and parents; clarify we thank Allah first and also thank people.

teach.heading: Share what we know
teach.note: Pairs: tell your partner one sentence about Allah. Choose children to share. Praise accurate sentences.

practice: Fill: Allah made the ______ (accept any creation).
Hold up one finger and say 'Allah is One'.
independent: Draw or write three things Allah made and label them
Tick true or false: Allah has a partner / Allah is One / Allah made everything
Say or trace the English meaning of Surah al-Ikhlas ayah 1
exit: How many gods are there?
Finish the sentence: Allah is ______
lessons.homework: Say the first two ayat of Surah al-Ikhlas to your family and tell them what 'Allah is One' means.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: use gesture (one finger) and picture cards; stress repetition. Stretch: explain why we say 'Allah has no partner'.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Allah, the One and Only
lessons.title: The beautiful names of Allah
objectives: Know Allah has beautiful names
Say and understand three names: Ar-Rahman, Ar-Raheem, Al-Khaliq
Link a name to something Allah has done
starter: Show one finger and say what it means.

teach.heading: Names of Allah
bullets: The Qur'an tells us to call on Him by them
Each name teaches us about Allah
teach.note: Allah says that to Him belong the best names, so call on Him by them (7:180). Explain the names show us who Allah is. Do not compare Allah to people or things; His names suit His greatness.

teach.heading: Ar-Rahman, Ar-Raheem
teach.note: Point to Bismillah: it contains both names. Ask where else children hear it. Explain that Allah's mercy is bigger than any person's mercy. Keep this age-appropriate.

teach.heading: Al-Khaliq
bullets: Allah created the earth and sky
teach.note: Show pictures of creation. Ask children to name a creation. Misconception: people 'create' like Allah. We make things from what Allah created; only Allah brings things into being.

teach.heading: Use the names
bullets: We make dua using His names
teach.note: Model simple dua: Ya Allah. Ask children for a short dua using a name. Praise sincere ones. The Prophet ﷺ said Allah has ninety-nine names; whoever learns and understands them enters Paradise (Bukhari and Muslim). Say simply: learning His names is a good deed.

teach.heading: Names chant
teach.note: Chant with actions (hands on heart for mercy, arms wide for creation). Repeat twice.

practice: Fill: Allah is the One. Allah is the ______ (Creator).
independent: Match each name to its meaning: Ar-Rahman / Ar-Raheem / Al-Khaliq
Draw something from creation and write 'Al-Khaliq' next to it
Complete: Allah is Ar-Rahman. I should be ______ (kind)
exit: Which name means the Creator?
Where do we say Ar-Rahman and Ar-Raheem?
lessons.homework: Learn the three names and say them to a family member with their meanings.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: name cards with pictures; echo reading. Stretch: link each name to an example from your day.

lessons.unit: Unit 1: Allah, the One and Only
lessons.title: Allah sees and hears us
objectives: Know Allah hears and sees everything
Say how this helps us do good
Make a simple dua
starter: Name Allah's three names we learned.

teach.heading: Allah hears
teach.note: Whisper a word and ask who can hear. Explain that Allah hears even the quietest dua. Name: As-Sami', the All-Hearing.

teach.heading: Allah sees
bullets: Allah sees even in the dark
teach.note: Name: Al-Basir. Use a darkness example: even when no one else is there, Allah sees. Make it positive: Allah sees our kindness. Avoid frightening children.

teach.heading: Musa and Harun
bullets: Allah told Musa and Harun not to be afraid
Allah said: I am with you, I hear and I see
teach.note: In Surah Ta-Ha, Allah told Musa and Harun not to fear because He hears and sees (20:46). Tell the story briefly: they were sent to Fir'awn. Allah's hearing and seeing gave them courage.

teach.heading: Good choices
bullets: Do good even when nobody is watching
teach.note: Scenario: you find a pencil that is not yours. No one is looking. What do you do? Praise answers that return it. Link to honesty.

teach.heading: Our dua
teach.note: Teach a simple dua: Rabbi zidni 'ilma (My Lord, increase me in knowledge, 20:114). Children echo. Explain it is a short dua from the Qur'an; we can ask Allah in our own words too.

practice: What do we call Allah when we see something amazing?
Say Allah's name 'Ar-Rahman' and what it means.
independent: Draw a dua card with a border pattern and write one dua in English
Tick the good choices when no one is looking
Write or say: Allah hears me and Allah sees me
exit: Which name means the All-Hearing?
What should we do when no one is watching?
lessons.homework: Make a short dua with your own words before bed and say Ameen.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: dua frame 'Ya Allah, please help me with ___'. Stretch: explain how knowing Allah sees us helps us be good.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: The early life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
lessons.title: Born in Makkah: Muhammad ﷺ and his family
objectives: Know where and when Muhammad ﷺ was born
Name his parents and grandfather
Know he was an orphan who was cared for

keywords.def: a child whose parents have died

starter: What do we say after the Prophet's name?

teach.heading: Makkah
bullets: Makkah is a city in Arabia
Ibrahim and Ismail built the Kaaba
teach.note: Show a map. Locate Makkah. The Qur'an tells us Ibrahim and Ismail raised the foundations of the House (2:127). Explain the Kaaba is where Muslims face to pray.

teach.heading: Muhammad ﷺ is born
bullets: Born in the 'Year of the Elephant'
Born in Makkah, in the tribe of Quraysh
teach.note: Explain that he was born in Makkah, in the Year of the Elephant, on a Monday (he ﷺ said Monday is the day he was born, Muslim). Explain the story of the elephant army is in Surah al-Fil (105). Do not give the exact date; scholars differ and say that.

teach.heading: His family
teach.note: His father Abdullah died before he was born. His mother Aminah passed away when he was a small child. His grandfather Abdul-Muttalib cared for him, then his uncle Abu Talib. Be gentle with children who may have lost relatives.

teach.heading: The kind nurse
bullets: He lived with Halimah in the desert
Arab families did this for healthy air
teach.note: Explain the Arab custom: babies were sent to desert families. Halimah as-Sa'diyyah nursed him. Keep to this simple fact. Ask: who looks after you?

teach.heading: Allah cared for him
bullets: He was an orphan but Allah cared for him
Allah says He found him an orphan and gave him shelter
teach.note: Surah ad-Duha (93:6) says: did He not find you an orphan and give you refuge? Tell children we should be kind to orphans. Remember the Prophet ﷺ said he and the caretaker of an orphan will be like two fingers in Jannah (Bukhari). Hold up two fingers.

practice: Which city is the Kaaba in?
What do we say after his name?
independent: Put the family names in order: Abdullah, Aminah, Abdul-Muttalib (match to labels)
Draw the Kaaba and label it 'Makkah'
True or false: Muhammad ﷺ was born in Madinah
exit: Where was Muhammad ﷺ born?
Name one person who cared for him.
lessons.homework: Ask a family member about orphans and say one kind thing we can do for them.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: family tree picture; map pointing. Stretch: explain what being an orphan means.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: The early life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
lessons.title: Al-Amin: the trustworthy one
objectives: Know that Muhammad ﷺ was called Al-Amin
Know what trustworthy means
Show a trustworthy action
starter: Who cared for him after his mother died?

teach.heading: As-Sadiq al-Amin
bullets: This is what Makkah called him
teach.note: The seerah reports that the Quraysh called him al-Amin. Ask: what does it mean when people trust you? Link to Reception truthfulness.

teach.heading: A job to do
bullets: People kept their things safe with him
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said Allah sent no prophet who did not shepherd sheep (Bukhari). Explain shepherding taught care and patience. Keep the trading story simple: he was honest in trade.

teach.heading: Why be trustworthy?
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught that truthfulness leads to righteousness and righteousness leads to Paradise (Bukhari and Muslim). Read slowly. Ask: what does truthful mean?

teach.heading: Keep a trust
bullets: Keep a secret that is good to keep
teach.note: Role-play lending a pencil. Ask: how do you feel if it is returned? If it is broken? Praise sorry and repair.

teach.heading: Trust game
teach.note: A pretend treasure box passed to a trusted child. Ask them to say how they kept it safe. Reinforce amanah.

independent: Draw a trustworthy action and write one sentence
Match: truthful / trustworthy / kind to the right example
Colour the child who keeps a trust
exit: What was Muhammad ﷺ called by the people of Makkah?
What does Al-Amin mean?
lessons.homework: Do one thing this week that shows you can be trusted, and tell a family member.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: pictures for each action; sentence frame 'I am trustworthy when I ___'. Stretch: write why trust matters in friendships.

lessons.unit: Unit 2: The early life of Prophet Muhammad ﷺ
lessons.title: Cave Hira and the first revelation
objectives: Retell the first revelation simply
Know the first word was 'Iqra' (read)
Know the Prophet ﷺ was 40 years old

keywords.def: Allah's message sent to a prophet

starter: What do we call the trustworthy one?

teach.heading: Time to think
bullets: Muhammad ﷺ went to the Cave of Hira
It is on a mountain near Makkah
teach.note: Show a picture of the mountain. Use a map or photo; no pictures of the Prophet ﷺ. Explain he went there to be quiet and think. Do not claim details beyond the authentic accounts.

teach.heading: Jibril comes
bullets: The angel Jibril came to him
teach.note: The story is in Bukhari. The Prophet ﷺ said he could not read; Jibril squeezed him and repeated three times. Tell it gently and simply. The first ayat: Iqra' bismi rabbika alladhi khalaq (96:1).

teach.heading: Surah al-Alaq
bullets: Read in the name of your Lord who created
He created man from a clot
Your Lord is the Most Generous
teach.note: Say the meaning of 96:1-3 in English. Do not ask children to recite. Highlight that the first command is to read and learn. Link to school.

teach.heading: Khadijah helps
teach.note: Khadijah said Allah would never disgrace him because he keeps family ties, helps the poor and is honest (Bukhari). Summarise in child-friendly words. Ask: how can we comfort a friend?

teach.heading: A new journey
teach.note: Keep to: revelation came over about 23 years in Makkah and Madinah. Link to what the children are learning in Qur'an. Praise attention.

practice: Name Allah's name 'the Creator' in Arabic.
What do we say after the Prophet's name?
independent: Sequence 4 pictures: cave, Jibril, going home, Khadijah
Write or draw the first word of revelation (Iqra) and what it means
Answer: why is learning important in Islam?
exit: What was the first word Jibril said?
Who comforted the Prophet ﷺ?
lessons.homework: Tell someone at home the story of the first revelation in your own words.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: story sequence cards. Stretch: explain why 'read' was the first command.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Islam and the five pillars
lessons.title: The five pillars of Islam
lessons.bigQuestion: What would happen to a house if one of its pillars was taken away?
objectives: To understand that Islam is built on five pillars, like a strong building
successCriteria: Most: match each pillar to something a Muslim does
Some: explain why a building needs all of its pillars
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: Islam gives each day a shape through the five pillars

keywords.def: a strong post that holds a building up
our way of life: obeying Allah
saying Allah is One and Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger
the prayer five times a day

hook.text: What would happen to a house if one of its pillars was taken away?
hook.a: It would wobble or fall down. Islam has five pillars and we need all five.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'I did not create jinn and mankind except to worship Me' (adh-Dhariyat 51:56). The five pillars show us how to worship Allah.

starter.q: Who made you and everything around you?

teach.heading: Islam is built on five
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said Islam is built on five
Like five pillars holding up a building
teach.note: Hold up five fingers. Tell the class the Prophet ﷺ taught that Islam is built on five things (Bukhari 8, Muslim 16). Build a 'house' with five pencils under a book: take one away and watch it tip.

teach.heading: The five pillars on five fingers
teach.note: Point to each finger in turn and say the pillar together. Pupils copy on camera.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the Teams poll. Praise everyone who tries.

check.q: Which pillar is praying five times a day?
check.why: Salah is prayer. Hajj is the journey to Makkah; zakah is giving.

practice.q: Say the five pillars on your fingers.
practice.model: I hold my thumb: shahadah. Pointer: salah. Middle: zakah. Ring: sawm. Little finger: Hajj.

independent.q: Draw a building with five pillars. Write one pillar on each.
independent.a: Five pillars labelled: shahadah, salah, zakah, sawm, Hajj
independent.model: Teacher draws a roof with the word Islam, then five lines underneath and writes 'shahadah' on the first.

independent.q: Extend: tick the pillar you can do every day.
Stretch: why does the house need all five pillars?
independent.a: Without one, it is not complete and strong.

exit.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?
Back to our ponder: what happens if a pillar is missing?
exit.a: The building is not strong. We need all five pillars.

lessons.homework: Show your family the five pillars on your fingers and teach them to one person.
lessons.send: SEND: five-finger picture card with one word on each. EAL: say each pillar after the teacher. Stretch: say what each pillar means in a sentence.
resources: School-approved children's Islamic Studies book (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Five pencils and a book (to model the pillars)

pictures.alt: Rows of strong pillars inside a building
The Ka'bah in Makkah, the place of Hajj

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Islam and the five pillars
lessons.title: The shahadah and the five daily prayers
lessons.bigQuestion: If you could talk to Allah five times every day, what would you say to Him?
objectives: To understand what the shahadah means and know the names of the five daily prayers
successCriteria: All: say the shahadah with the teacher
Most: name the five prayers in order
Some: match each prayer to a time of day
lessons.smsc: Spiritual: salah is a daily meeting with Allah

keywords.def: the words that say Allah is One and Muhammad ﷺ is His Messenger

hook.text: If you could talk to Allah five times every day, what would you say to Him?
hook.a: Thank you, help me, forgive me. Salah is our special time with Allah.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'Indeed, prayer has been decreed upon the believers at fixed times' (an-Nisa 4:103).

starter.q: How many pillars of Islam are there?

teach.heading: The shahadah
bullets: Allah is the only One we worship
Muslims say it and believe it
teach.note: Say the shahadah slowly with pupils: أَشْهَدُ أَنْ لَا إِلٰهَ إِلَّا اللَّهُ وَأَشْهَدُ أَنَّ مُحَمَّدًا رَسُولُ اللَّهِ. Explain in simple words: I say for sure there is no god but Allah, and Muhammad ﷺ is the Messenger of Allah.

teach.heading: Five prayers through the day
teach.note: Show the day on a line: dark, sunrise, midday, afternoon, sunset, night. Pupils point as you say each prayer.

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll; then ask pupils to show the prayer on their hands.

check.why: Maghrib is at sunset. Fajr is at dawn and Dhuhr at midday.

practice.q: Say the five prayers in order.
practice.model: I start with the morning: Fajr. Then midday: Dhuhr. Afternoon: Asr. Sunset: Maghrib. Night: Isha.

practice.q: Which prayer do we pray before school?

independent.q: Draw five suns or moons for a day and label each prayer.
independent.model: Teacher draws a small sun coming up and writes Fajr under it, then a high sun for Dhuhr.

independent.q: Extend: which prayer is in the dark night?
Stretch: what does the shahadah say about Allah?
independent.a: There is no god but Allah: He is the only One we worship.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what is one thing you can say to Allah in your prayer?
exit.a: For example: thank You, Allah, for my family.

lessons.homework: Listen for each adhan at home this week and tell your family which prayer it is.
lessons.send: SEND: picture strip of the sky at five times of day. EAL: repeat the prayer names. Stretch: say how many prayers are in a week (35).
resources: School-approved children's Islamic Studies book (TO CONFIRM title with the Islamic Studies lead)
Shahadah card in Arabic with meaning
Pupil PDF worksheet: my prayer day

pictures.alt: The sky at dawn, the time of Fajr
The sky at sunset, the time of Maghrib
A prayer mat ready for salah

lessons.unit: Unit 3: The pillars of Islam and salah
lessons.title: Wudu step by step
objectives: Say the steps of wudu in order
Know why we make wudu
Say the dua after wudu

keywords.def: washing in a set order to get ready to pray
one after another in the right place
each main part is washed three times

starter: What do we say at the start of wudu?
Why do we wash before salah?

teach.heading: Wudu: Part 1
teach.note: Demonstrate with a bowl or video. Each washing is three times. The Prophet ﷺ taught wudu by doing it (Bukhari and Muslim, Uthman). Do not rush.

teach.heading: Wudu: Part 2
teach.note: Right then left for arms. Emphasise gentle. Check hair, nose and elbows are included.

teach.heading: Wudu: Part 3
teach.note: Children mime. The head is wiped, not washed. Right then left for feet. Misconception: washing the head like the face; we wipe it with wet hands.

teach.heading: After wudu
bullets: 'wa ash-hadu anna Muhammadan abduhu wa rasuluhu'
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ taught that whoever makes wudu well and then says the shahadah has the gates of Jannah opened (Muslim). Say it simply. Echo the words.

teach.heading: Wudu relay
teach.note: Pairs: one acts, one checks the order with a card set. Switch roles. Collect any errors for review.

practice: Show the first step of wudu.
independent: Put the wudu steps in order (8 cards)
Draw and label one step of wudu
Say the dua after wudu to a partner
exit: What do we do first in wudu?
What do we say after wudu?
lessons.homework: Make wudu with an adult and say the steps in order.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: step cards with pictures; mime. Stretch: say the dua in Arabic and English.

lessons.title: Shukr: being thankful
objectives: Know Allah gives us many blessings
Show thanks to Allah and people
Know gratitude makes blessings grow
starter: What do we say after wudu?
What do we say after eating?

teach.heading: Too many to count
teach.note: Allah says that if we try to count His blessings we cannot (16:18). Children list blessings until you cannot write more. The Al-Baseerah KS1 quiz asked: what blessings has Allah given us? Use this as a class chart.

teach.heading: Allah increases us
bullets: Allah says: if you are grateful, I will increase you
teach.note: Surah Ibrahim 14:7: if you are grateful, I will surely increase you. Explain 'increase' as giving more good. Link to thanking parents.

teach.heading: Thank people too
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ taught us to thank people
'He who does not thank people does not thank Allah'
teach.note: This hadith is in Abu Dawud and at-Tirmidhi. Teach the phrase JazakAllahu khayran: may Allah reward you with good. Practise with pairs.

teach.heading: Showing thanks
teach.note: Ask: how can we use our hands to show thanks? Help, write, make dua. Link to the Al-Baseerah Salah talk: do not use Allah's gifts to do wrong.

teach.heading: Thank-you cards
teach.note: Children plan a card for parents or teacher. Check they write a full sentence.

independent: Make a blessings list: write five things Allah has given you
Write a thank-you note to someone at home
Match: 'thanks to Allah' / 'thanks to people'
exit: What do we say to a person who helps us?
Can we count Allah's blessings?
lessons.homework: Give your thank-you note and say JazakAllahu khayran.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: sentence frame 'Thank you for ___'. Stretch: write two sentences on why gratitude matters.

lessons.title: Truthfulness and honesty
objectives: Know that Islam teaches us to tell the truth
Explain the hadith about truthfulness
Choose honesty in a tricky situation

keywords.def: doing what is good and right

teach.heading: The hadith
bullets: The Prophet ﷺ said: truthfulness leads to righteousness
teach.note: Bukhari and Muslim (Ibn Mas'ud). Read it slowly: the truthful person keeps telling the truth until he is written with Allah as truthful. Explain in kid language.

teach.heading: Why people lie
teach.note: Discuss reasons children might hide the truth. Reassure: honesty brings forgiveness faster. Do not shame any child.

teach.heading: Telling the truth bravely
teach.note: Use scenario cards. Role-play one. Show how to say 'I made a mistake and I am sorry'. Praise bravery.

teach.heading: Keeping your word
teach.note: Link to Al-Amin. Ask: why do people trust someone who keeps promises? Link to the Prophet's trustworthiness.

teach.heading: Honesty pledge
teach.note: Class makes a simple pledge. Display on the wall. Do not require children to sign; keep it voluntary.

independent: Act a scene: a child breaks something. What do they say?
Write a rule about telling the truth
Complete the hadith meaning sentence: Truthfulness leads to ______
exit: What does truthfulness lead to?
What do we say if we make a mistake?
lessons.homework: Tell a family member about the hadith on truthfulness.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: scenario pictures and sentence frames. Stretch: write your own hadith explanation.

lessons.title: Looking after Allah's gifts (amanah)
objectives: Know that everything belongs to Allah
Understand we are trusted to look after what we have
Choose ways to care for gifts

keywords.def: something we are trusted to look after
taking care of what we are given

teach.heading: Who owns everything?
bullets: The heavens and the earth belong to Allah
We are given it to use well
teach.note: Surah al-Baqarah 2:284: to Allah belongs what is in the heavens and earth. Use the Al-Baseerah bike story: if someone lends you a bike to fix and clean and you break it, is that good? Discuss.

teach.heading: Our bodies
bullets: We keep them clean and safe
We use them to worship and help
teach.note: Link to wudu and healthy food. Ask how children look after bodies. Keep sensitive; avoid shaming anyone's body.

teach.heading: Our things
teach.note: Show broken versus cared-for items. Ask what we do if we break something. Say sorry and fix if possible.

teach.heading: Our world
teach.note: Link to the Qur'an: Allah says do not be wasteful (7:31). Keep the phrase simple. Ask children to give one way to save water.

teach.heading: Amanah chart
bullets: Say how to care for them
teach.note: Children choose one gift and a caring action. Share with a partner.

independent: Draw one gift from Allah and write how you will look after it
Sort cards: caring / not caring
Complete: Allah owns ______ and I will ______
exit: Who owns everything?
How do we show thanks for gifts?
lessons.homework: Look after one gift from Allah this week and tell us how.
lessons.send: SEND/EAL: picture sort and frames. Stretch: explain the bike example in your own words.

lessons.unit: Spring 1: Islam and the five pillars
lessons.title: Zakah and sadaqah: giving to people in need
lessons.bigQuestion: If you had one apple and your friend had none, what would you do?
objectives: To understand why Muslims give zakah and sadaqah to people in need
successCriteria: All: say what zakah and sadaqah are
Most: give two ways a child can give sadaqah
Some: name sawm and Hajj as the last two pillars
lessons.smsc: Moral and social: caring for people in need

keywords.def: money Muslims must give each year to people in need
any good thing we give or do to help
the visit to the Ka'bah in Makkah

hook.text: If you had one apple and your friend had none, what would you do?
hook.a: Share it. Islam teaches us to give to people who need help.

islamicLink.text: Allah says: 'And establish prayer and give zakah' (al-Baqarah 2:43).

teach.heading: Zakah: the third pillar
bullets: Muslims with enough money must give some
It goes to poor and needy people
Giving makes our money clean and blessed
teach.note: Use real coins: pretend you have 40 coins and give 1 away. Keep it simple: grown-ups with enough money give a small part every year.

teach.heading: Sadaqah: everyone can give
bullets: Sadaqah is any good we give
Helping and kind words count too
teach.note: The Prophet ﷺ said to protect yourselves from the Fire even with half a date (Bukhari and Muslim). Ask: what can a child give? Toys, help, a smile, a kind word.

teach.heading: Sort it
teach.note: Read each card. Pupils show 1 for zakah or 2 for sadaqah on their fingers.

cards: A grown-up gives part of their savings each year
Money given every year to the poor
I give my old coat to someone cold

teach.heading: Quick check
teach.note: Launch the poll.

check.q: Which one can every child do?
check.why: Sadaqah can be any good deed, so every child can give it.

practice.q: Say two kinds of sadaqah a child can give.
practice.a: For example: share food, help someone
practice.model: I can share my snack with my brother. I can carry the shopping for Grandma. Both are sadaqah.

practice.q: Fasting in Ramadan is the pillar called ...

independent.q: Draw two hands giving. Write one way you will give sadaqah this week.
independent.a: For example: I will give my toy car to my cousin.
independent.model: Teacher draws two hands and writes: I will help Dad wash the dishes.

independent.q: Stretch: why does Allah love it when we give?
independent.a: It helps people and shows we care, and Allah rewards it.

exit.q: Back to our ponder: what would you do with the apple, and why?
exit.a: Share it, because Islam teaches us to give.

lessons.homework: Do one act of sadaqah at home and tell the class about it next lesson.
lessons.send: SEND: picture cards of giving. EAL: model sentence 'I can give ...'. Stretch: explain the difference between zakah and sadaqah.
